title: The Dinosaur Shirt
can_do: 用颜色或明显特征说清楚自己要哪一个。
trigger: Dad offers two red shirts, one striped and one with a dinosaur, so color alone does not identify Child's choice.
stretch_response: The one with the dinosaur, please.
repair_response: No, the one with the stars.
essential_props: two red shirts: one striped and one with a dinosaur

turns.speaker: dad
turns.line: Time to choose a shirt. Which one do you want?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: The one with the dinosaur, please.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Thanks, Dad. That's the one I wanted.

replay_cards.title: Pick a pajama top
replay_cards.change: Choose between two blue pajama tops, one with stars and one with stripes
replay_cards.challenge: Child asks, 'Can I have the blue one, please?' Dad checks the striped top. Child says, 'No, the one with the stars.' Dad confirms the star pattern, hands him that top, and helps him get ready to change.

replay_cards.title: Find the cup
replay_cards.change: Choose between two green cups, one with a handle and one without
replay_cards.challenge: Child requests the green cup. Mom asks which one; he identifies the handle. Mom points to that cup for confirmation, then hands it to him for his drink.

parent_support: Show only the two red choices. If his color choice still fits both, ask about their visible patterns.
Accept any detail that truly identifies the object, then check once before handing it over.
Keep the yellow T-shirt on during the recorded scene; he receives the dinosaur shirt and agrees to get dressed next. A small smile or nod is enough.
